title: I Designed A Custom PCB To Avoid Pressing A Button Three Times
excerpt: My night light always booted up too bright, so I designed a PCB that presses its button for me.
content_html:
It’s hard for me to explain why, but ever since I can remember I hated sleeping in full darkness. Perhaps it’s to do with where I was born, where even during the night I could see street lights. Maybe it has to do with me just being a big baby.

But because of also being a nerd I love to automate all sorts of things like this. I use Home Assistant to control basically everything smart around the house, and one of the automations I have is to turn on a dumb night light using a Zigbee wall plug. Basically when my phone goes into the sleep focus mode, it tells Home Assistant that, which in turn runs a few automations around the house, one being turning on this night light.

All great right? Well, not really.

The light that always starts too bright#

I have bought a cheap night light from the internet that has a button and a switch. The switch basically tells it if it should turn on automatically at night (no thank you, I want that control myself, so the switch is always off), and the button basically jumps between the intensity levels supported.

Well, here’s the issue. First of all, it doesn’t start on intensity 1. It starts at 3. Then you press once, goes to 4, then again, goes to 5, then yet again and it goes to 1. So every single night when I went to bed, I would have to press that button 3 times because otherwise the light was way too bright.

Opening it up#

I have opened the light to take a look inside, maybe I can gain some information about the chips used there, maybe there is a potentiometer that I can use. But no.

The chips didn’t have their names visible.

Someone online mentioned that these lights all use the same ICs basically and there’s this trick where if you hold down the switch button for like 10 seconds you set in the EEPROM the new default value (instead of 3). Not on mine. I have tried everything.

So I gave up and just bought a smart night light that I can adjust from Home Assistant, and my nights were perfect since. Thank you for reading. Tune in next time for when I buy the solution to my next problem!

Pressing the button with a chip#

Nope. I did what any normal person would do and went down a rabbit hole of understanding how the circuit worked. In reality it wasn’t anything super complicated, and I realised that my actual best bet at solving this would be a microcontroller that could just press the button for me so to say.

I had a few in mind, some that were in the room with me such as a Wemos D1 Mini (the ESP8266 one) and a Raspberry Pi Zero, but they all had some issues. The night light has no transformer in it, it drops the mains voltage with a capacitor instead, and that kind of supply can only give you a few milliamps. An ESP8266 wants hundreds of milliamps the moment it boots and turns its radio on, and the Pi Zero is a whole Linux computer that needs to boot an operating system before it can do anything at all, so both of them would have needed their own power supply, or a big reservoir capacitor and extra circuitry to survive the boot spike. Neither of those is “solder three wires and be done”.

So I decided upon using the ATtiny85. The reason was that this is a super well known chip, from the same AVR family the classic Arduinos use, so you can write the code in the Arduino IDE exactly like you would for an Arduino. And it uses basically 0 power. It’s so low it’s hard to even analogize, but I’ll give it a go: running at 1 MHz it pulls less than a milliamp, and once it goes to sleep it drops to microamps, which is about what a quartz watch uses to keep ticking. The LED in the night light uses thousands of times more than that.

Now the issue is that I can’t just hook this up to power, ground, and the button and be done with it. I also need:

  • An HT7333 voltage regulator, because the rail inside the light sits at 8.3 V and the ATtiny wants 3.3 V.
  • A 2N3904 transistor, which is the part that actually presses the button. It shorts the button’s signal leg to ground, exactly like my finger does.
  • A 1 kΩ resistor between the chip and the transistor, so the chip only ever drives a tiny current into it.
  • A 10 kΩ resistor to hold the transistor off while everything powers up, otherwise you get a stray press at boot and the light jumps to a random brightness.
  • Three small capacitors, which smooth out the power going into the regulator and the chip.
  • A 3 pin header for the only three wires that leave the board: power, ground, and the wire that goes to the button.

At the end as you can see there’s a ton of stuff, so I had this brilliant idea of spending even more time and money and creating a PCB for it? Why? Well, cause it would be useful for anyone that needs something like this in their life where they can just have something press a simple switch button for them X amount of times. I needed this tons of times myself, for example the stupid AC…

Another reason is because I’ve never made my own PCB and I wanted to learn how to do it, and what the process could be. And third reason is because it’s genuinely just cool. If you don’t think so you’re in the wrong place.

Designing it in EasyEDA#

As I’ve said I’ve never used anything like this to make PCBs, but after some LLMing I have decided to try EasyEDA. Honestly the process was much simpler than I expected. You basically need to lay down a circuit diagram of sorts explaining all the chips and stuff you need, and then the tool lets you show connections, such as you can see in the image where I have the connections labeled as “GND” or “3V3” etc. Every one of those that has the same name will be connected then by the router. Neat!

Then I had to basically tell the tool what the actual items there are. Like actually the real life part. This helped with positioning on the PCB, as well as with the bill of materials later on.

Once you get to the PCB design you have full control over where things go, if you want to print stuff onto it (I printed a cool open source hardware logo and my username on mine). You will also have control about where things are routed, where things are positioned, what the shape of the PCB is, and so on.

Mine is obviously simple and I’m just scratching the surface. It’s single layered, I didn’t bother with super intricate lines, I didn’t have to worry about how long lines are or if I need to compensate on how wobbly they are or anything, but you CAN do all that and that’s super cool!

Getting it made#

Next step was going to the company that ends up making these PCBs for you! In my case that company was JLCPCB. They have not sponsored this or anything, it’s just what I ended up using and honestly it was very cool because you can then select the real life components you want on the board, and if you want them to solder them for you, or if you are happy doing it yourself.

In my case I only really needed one board, and the minimum you can order is 5, so I opted into soldering things myself, mostly, but for the capacitors and resistors I opted for them to do it because they are EXTREMELY small and the price for them to do it is negligible.

I have then put in the order and 4 days later I had the board in my hand. Honestly super neat, hard to put into words but I think I’m addicted now. I need to make more real life things!!!

Programming the ATtiny#

I have jumped at soldering the rest of the components in, the wires, and tested my simplistic code on the ATtiny on a breadboard to see if it works, and it did.

I actually used a Raspberry Pi 3 to program it. A blank ATtiny has no bootloader on it, so you can’t just plug it into USB like an Arduino, it needs a proper programmer. The Pi’s GPIO pins can do exactly that job with avrdude, so it’s six jumper wires from the Pi’s header to the chip and one command.

Instead of wiring it straight to the light for the first test, I put an LED on the output pin and watched it blink the sequence out. Three blinks, then nothing forever (in the video it’s actually blinking 4 times, because I only realised later on that I needed 3, whoops).

Soldering it into the light#

Then I have wired it up, and soldered it to my night light. It was very hard to do, everything is extremely tiny and my soldering work is not something I’m super proud of, but in the end it worked!

One weird thing is that the big capacitor on the board was actually inverted, no clue why. Luckily I checked with my multimeter.

One thing worth saying out loud here, because this light has no transformer in it: once my board is wired in, the whole thing is connected to mains. That means you flash the chip before it goes in, and you never plug a USB cable or a Pi into it again afterwards.

The result#

Here you can see it in all of its glory.

“What is that shadow there? Are those wires inside that you can see? Eww, this project sucks!”

First of all, who hurt you? Second of all, I agree but I don’t wanna risk breaking those solder joints because I will cry. And third of all I don’t really care, I’m in bed and it lights up. Those are behind the diffusion panel, they don’t show up on the wall in the room, I’m a happy camper.

Now when the watch tells my phone I am in bed ready to sleep, the phone tells Home Assistant, which tells the switch to turn on, which turns on the night light, which turns on my concoction that presses the button 3 times with a slight delay (to not bug out) and it brings up a huge smile on my face.

Take it and make your own#

It’s all up on GitHub at tymscar/button-presser, MIT licensed, so do whatever you want with it. The gerbers are in there if you want this exact board made, along with the bill of materials, the schematic, and the handful of lines of C that run on the chip.

The README also has the two multimeter checks you need to do first, because this only works on devices with a 4 V to 12 V rail inside and a button that shorts to ground when you press it. That covers a lot of cheap gadgets, but not all of them. If your device runs off mains like mine does, read the safety bit before you start.

So go out there and make your own silly PCB for something. It’s very fun and rewarding. See you next time!

sentences.zh: ESP8266 在启动和打开无线电时需要数百毫安的电流，而 Pi Zero 是一个完整的 Linux 计算机，需要启动操作系统才能执行任何操作，因此它们都需要自己的电源，或者一个大的存储电容器和额外的电路来承受启动尖峰。

sentences.en: Neither of those is “solder three wires and be done”.
sentences.zh: 这些都不是“焊三根线就可以了”。

blocks.html_en: So I decided upon using the ATtiny85. The reason was that this is a super well known chip, from the same AVR family the classic Arduinos use, so you can write the code in the Arduino IDE exactly like you would for an Arduino. And it uses basically 0 power. It’s so low it’s hard to even analogize, but I’ll give it a go: running at 1 MHz it pulls less than a milliamp, and once it goes to sleep it drops to microamps, which is about what a quartz watch uses to keep ticking. The LED in the night light uses thousands of times more than that.

sentences.en: So I decided upon using the ATtiny85.
sentences.zh: 所以我决定使用 ATtiny85。

sentences.en: The reason was that this is a super well known chip, from the same AVR family the classic Arduinos use, so you can write the code in the Arduino IDE exactly like you would for an Arduino.
sentences.zh: 原因是，这是一款非常知名的芯片，与经典 Arduino 使用的 AVR 系列相同，因此您可以在 Arduino IDE 中编写代码，就像在 Arduino 中编写代码一样。

sentences.en: And it uses basically 0 power.
sentences.zh: 而且它使用的电量基本为0。

sentences.en: It’s so low it’s hard to even analogize, but I’ll give it a go: running at 1 MHz it pulls less than a milliamp, and once it goes to sleep it drops to microamps, which is about what a quartz watch uses to keep ticking.
sentences.zh: 它是如此之低，甚至很难类比，但我会尝试一下：以 1 MHz 运行时，它的电流不到一毫安，一旦进入睡眠状态，它就会降至微安，这大约是石英表用来保持滴答作响的电流。

sentences.en: The LED in the night light uses thousands of times more than that.
sentences.zh: 夜灯中的LED使用量比这个多数千倍。

blocks.html_en: Now the issue is that I can’t just hook this up to power, ground, and the button and be done with it. I also need:

sentences.en: Now the issue is that I can’t just hook this up to power, ground, and the button and be done with it.
sentences.zh: 现在的问题是，我不能仅仅将其连接到电源、接地和按钮上就可以完成它。

sentences.en: I also need:
sentences.zh: 我还需要：

blocks.html_en: • An HT7333 voltage regulator, because the rail inside the light sits at 8.3 V and the ATtiny wants 3.3 V.

sentences.en: An HT7333 voltage regulator, because the rail inside the light sits at 8.3 V and the ATtiny wants 3.3 V.
sentences.zh: HT7333 稳压器，因为灯内的电压轨为 8.3 V，而 ATtiny 需要 3.3 V。

blocks.html_en: • A 2N3904 transistor, which is the part that actually presses the button. It shorts the button’s signal leg to ground, exactly like my finger does.

sentences.en: A 2N3904 transistor, which is the part that actually presses the button.
sentences.zh: 2N3904晶体管，这是实际按下按钮的部分。

sentences.en: It shorts the button’s signal leg to ground, exactly like my finger does.
sentences.zh: 它将按钮的信号腿短路到地，就像我的手指一样。

blocks.html_en: • A 1 kΩ resistor between the chip and the transistor, so the chip only ever drives a tiny current into it.

sentences.en: A 1 kΩ resistor between the chip and the transistor, so the chip only ever drives a tiny current into it.
sentences.zh: 芯片和晶体管之间有一个 1 kΩ 电阻，因此芯片仅向其中驱动微小电流。

blocks.html_en: • A 10 kΩ resistor to hold the transistor off while everything powers up, otherwise you get a stray press at boot and the light jumps to a random brightness.

sentences.en: A 10 kΩ resistor to hold the transistor off while everything powers up, otherwise you get a stray press at boot and the light jumps to a random brightness.
sentences.zh: 一个 10 kΩ 电阻器用于在一切通电时保持晶体管关闭，否则您会在启动时遇到误按，并且灯会跳到随机亮度。

blocks.html_en: • Three small capacitors, which smooth out the power going into the regulator and the chip.

sentences.en: Three small capacitors, which smooth out the power going into the regulator and the chip.
sentences.zh: 三个小电容器，可以平滑进入调节器和芯片的功率。

blocks.html_en: • A 3 pin header for the only three wires that leave the board: power, ground, and the wire that goes to the button.

sentences.en: A 3 pin header for the only three wires that leave the board: power, ground, and the wire that goes to the button.
sentences.zh: 3 针接头，用于离开电路板的仅有的三根电线：电源、接地和连接按钮的电线。

blocks.html_en: At the end as you can see there’s a ton of stuff, so I had this brilliant idea of spending even more time and money and creating a PCB for it? Why? Well, cause it would be useful for anyone that needs something like this in their life where they can just have something press a simple switch button for them X amount of times. I needed this tons of times myself, for example the stupid AC…

sentences.en: At the end as you can see there’s a ton of stuff, so I had this brilliant idea of spending even more time and money and creating a PCB for it?
sentences.zh: 最后你可以看到有很多东西，所以我有了一个绝妙的主意，那就是花费更多的时间和金钱并为其创建 PCB？

sentences.en: Why?

sentences.zh: 好吧，因为这对于生活中需要类似东西的任何人来说都是有用的，他们只需按一个简单的开关按钮 X 次即可。

sentences.en: I needed this tons of times myself, for example the stupid AC…
sentences.zh: 我自己需要很多次，例如愚蠢的空调......

blocks.html_en: Another reason is because I’ve never made my own PCB and I wanted to learn how to do it, and what the process could be. And third reason is because it’s genuinely just cool. If you don’t think so you’re in the wrong place.

sentences.en: Another reason is because I’ve never made my own PCB and I wanted to learn how to do it, and what the process could be.
sentences.zh: 另一个原因是因为我从未制作过自己的 PCB，我想学习如何制作以及流程是什么。

sentences.en: And third reason is because it’s genuinely just cool.
sentences.zh: 第三个原因是因为它真的很酷。

sentences.en: If you don’t think so you’re in the wrong place.

sentences.en: Designing it in EasyEDA#

blocks.html_en: As I’ve said I’ve never used anything like this to make PCBs, but after some LLMing I have decided to try EasyEDA. Honestly the process was much simpler than I expected. You basically need to lay down a circuit diagram of sorts explaining all the chips and stuff you need, and then the tool lets you show connections, such as you can see in the image where I have the connections labeled as “GND” or “3V3” etc. Every one of those that has the same name will be connected then by the router. Neat!

sentences.en: As I’ve said I’ve never used anything like this to make PCBs, but after some LLMing I have decided to try EasyEDA.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我从未使用过这样的东西来制作 PCB，但在学习了一些法学硕士学位后，我决定尝试 EasyEDA。

sentences.en: Honestly the process was much simpler than I expected.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这个过程比我想象的要简单得多。

sentences.en: You basically need to lay down a circuit diagram of sorts explaining all the chips and stuff you need, and then the tool lets you show connections, such as you can see in the image where I have the connections labeled as “GND” or “3V3” etc. Every one of those that has the same name will be connected then by the router.
sentences.zh: 您基本上需要制定一张电路图来解释您需要的所有芯片和东西，然后该工具可以让您显示连接，例如您可以在图像中看到，我将连接标记为“GND”或“3V3”等。每个具有相同名称的连接都将由路由器连接。

sentences.en: Neat!
sentences.zh: 整洁的！

blocks.html_en: Then I had to basically tell the tool what the actual items there are. Like actually the real life part. This helped with positioning on the PCB, as well as with the bill of materials later on.

sentences.en: Then I had to basically tell the tool what the actual items there are.
sentences.zh: 然后我基本上必须告诉工具实际的项目是什么。

sentences.en: Like actually the real life part.
sentences.zh: 就像现实生活中的部分一样。

sentences.en: This helped with positioning on the PCB, as well as with the bill of materials later on.
sentences.zh: 这有助于 PCB 上的定位以及随后的物料清单。

blocks.html_en: Once you get to the PCB design you have full control over where things go, if you want to print stuff onto it (I printed a cool open source hardware logo and my username on mine). You will also have control about where things are routed, where things are positioned, what the shape of the PCB is, and so on.

sentences.en: Once you get to the PCB design you have full control over where things go, if you want to print stuff onto it (I printed a cool open source hardware logo and my username on mine).
sentences.zh: 一旦你进行了 PCB 设计，如果你想在上面打印东西，你就可以完全控制事情的走向（我在我的上面打印了一个很酷的开源硬件徽标和我的用户名）。

sentences.en: You will also have control about where things are routed, where things are positioned, what the shape of the PCB is, and so on.
sentences.zh: 您还可以控制事物的布线位置、事物的位置、PCB 的形状等等。

sentences.en: Mine is obviously simple and I’m just scratching the surface.
sentences.zh: 我的显然很简单，我只是触及了表面。

sentences.en: Getting it made#
sentences.zh: 制作完成#

blocks.html_en: Next step was going to the company that ends up making these PCBs for you! In my case that company was JLCPCB. They have not sponsored this or anything, it’s just what I ended up using and honestly it was very cool because you can then select the real life components you want on the board, and if you want them to solder them for you, or if you are happy doing it yourself.

sentences.en: Next step was going to the company that ends up making these PCBs for you!
sentences.zh: 下一步是去最终为您制造这些 PCB 的公司！

sentences.zh: 就我而言，我只需要一块板，而您可以订购的最少数量是 5 个，所以我主要选择自己焊接东西，但对于电容器和电阻器，我选择让他们这样做，因为它们非常小，而且他们这样做的价格可以忽略不计。

blocks.html_en: Programming the ATtiny#

sentences.en: Programming the ATtiny#
sentences.zh: 对 ATtiny 进行编程#

blocks.html_en: I have jumped at soldering the rest of the components in, the wires, and tested my simplistic code on the ATtiny on a breadboard to see if it works, and it did.

sentences.en: I have jumped at soldering the rest of the components in, the wires, and tested my simplistic code on the ATtiny on a breadboard to see if it works, and it did.
sentences.zh: 我立即将其余组件焊接到电线中，并在面包板上的 ATtiny 上测试了我的简单代码，看看它是否有效，结果确实如此。

blocks.html_en: I actually used a Raspberry Pi 3 to program it. A blank ATtiny has no bootloader on it, so you can’t just plug it into USB like an Arduino, it needs a proper programmer. The Pi’s GPIO pins can do exactly that job with avrdude, so it’s six jumper wires from the Pi’s header to the chip and one command.

sentences.en: I actually used a Raspberry Pi 3 to program it.
sentences.zh: 我实际上使用了 Raspberry Pi 3 来对其进行编程。

sentences.en: A blank ATtiny has no bootloader on it, so you can’t just plug it into USB like an Arduino, it needs a proper programmer.
sentences.zh: 空白的 ATtiny 上没有引导加载程序，因此您不能像 Arduino 那样将其插入 USB，它需要一个合适的编程器。

sentences.en: The Pi’s GPIO pins can do exactly that job with avrdude, so it’s six jumper wires from the Pi’s header to the chip and one command.
sentences.zh: Pi 的 GPIO 引脚可以通过 avrdude 完成这项工作，因此从 Pi 的接头到芯片有 6 根跳线和一个命令。

blocks.html_en: Instead of wiring it straight to the light for the first test, I put an LED on the output pin and watched it blink the sequence out. Three blinks, then nothing forever (in the video it’s actually blinking 4 times, because I only realised later on that I needed 3, whoops).

sentences.en: Instead of wiring it straight to the light for the first test, I put an LED on the output pin and watched it blink the sequence out.
sentences.zh: 第一次测试时，我没有将其直接连接到灯上，而是在输出引脚上放置了一个 LED，然后看着它闪烁序列。

sentences.en: Three blinks, then nothing forever (in the video it’s actually blinking 4 times, because I only realised later on that I needed 3, whoops).
sentences.zh: 眨眼三下，然后就永远没有了（在视频中它实际上眨眼了 4 次，因为我后来才意识到我需要 3 次，哎呀）。

blocks.html_en: One thing worth saying out loud here, because this light has no transformer in it: once my board is wired in, the whole thing is connected to mains. That means you flash the chip before it goes in, and you never plug a USB cable or a Pi into it again afterwards.

sentences.zh: 这意味着您在插入芯片之前对其进行闪存，并且之后您再也不会将 USB 电缆或 Pi 插入其中。

content_html_zh:
我很难解释为什么，但自从我记事起，我就讨厌在完全黑暗的环境中睡觉。 也许这与我出生的地方有关，即使在晚上我也能看到路灯。 也许这与我只是一个大婴儿有关。

但因为我也是一个书呆子，所以我喜欢自动化各种类似的事情。 我使用 Home Assistant 来控制房子周围的所有智能设备，我拥有的自动化功能之一是使用 Zigbee 墙壁插头打开哑夜灯。 基本上，当我的手机进入睡眠焦点模式时，它会告诉家庭助理，然后家庭助理会在房子周围运行一些自动化操作，其中之一就是打开夜灯。

一切都很好吧？ 嗯，不是真的。

开始时的光总是太亮#

我从网上买了一个便宜的夜灯，有一个按钮和一个开关。 开关基本上告诉它是否应该在晚上自动打开（不，谢谢，我想要自己控制，所以开关总是关闭的），并且按钮基本上在支持的强度级别之间跳转。

好吧，这就是问题所在。 首先，它不是从强度 1 开始的。 3点开始。 然后按一次，转到 4，再按一次，转到 5，再按一次，转到 1。 所以每天晚上当我睡觉时，我都必须按那个按钮 3 次，否则灯太亮了。

打开它#

我打开灯看了看里面，也许我可以得到一些关于那里使用的芯片的信息，也许有一个电位器可以用。 但没有。

这些芯片的名字不可见。

网上有人提到，这些灯基本上都使用相同的 IC，并且有一个技巧，如果你按住开关按钮大约 10 秒，你就会在 EEPROM 中设置新的默认值（而不是 3）。 不在我的身上。 我已经尝试了一切。

所以我放弃了，只买了一个智能夜灯，我可以通过家庭助理进行调节，从那以后我的夜晚变得很完美。 感谢您的阅读。 下次我购买下一个问题的解决方案时请收听！

用芯片按下按钮#

没有。 我做了任何正常人都会做的事情，深入了解电路的工作原理。 事实上，这并不是什么超级复杂的事情，我意识到解决这个问题的最佳选择是使用一个微控制器，它可以帮我按下按钮。

我想到了一些，其中一些和我一起在房间里，例如 Wemos D1 Mini（ESP8266）和 Raspberry Pi Zero，但它们都有一些问题。 夜灯内部没有变压器，而是通过电容器来降低电源电压，而这种电源只能提供几毫安的电流。 ESP8266 在启动和打开无线电时需要数百毫安的电流，而 Pi Zero 是一个完整的 Linux 计算机，需要启动操作系统才能执行任何操作，因此它们都需要自己的电源，或者一个大的存储电容器和额外的电路来承受启动尖峰。 这些都不是“焊三根线就可以了”。

所以我决定使用 ATtiny85。 原因是，这是一款非常知名的芯片，与经典 Arduino 使用的 AVR 系列相同，因此您可以在 Arduino IDE 中编写代码，就像在 Arduino 中编写代码一样。 而且它使用的电量基本为0。 它是如此之低，甚至很难类比，但我会尝试一下：以 1 MHz 运行时，它的电流不到一毫安，一旦进入睡眠状态，它就会降至微安，这大约是石英表用来保持滴答作响的电流。 夜灯中的LED使用量比这个多数千倍。

现在的问题是，我不能仅仅将其连接到电源、接地和按钮上就可以完成它。 我还需要：

  • HT7333 稳压器，因为灯内的电压轨为 8.3 V，而 ATtiny 需要 3.3 V。
  • 2N3904晶体管，这是实际按下按钮的部分。 它将按钮的信号腿短路到地，就像我的手指一样。
  • 芯片和晶体管之间有一个 1 kΩ 电阻，因此芯片仅向其中驱动微小电流。
  • 一个 10 kΩ 电阻器用于在一切通电时保持晶体管关闭，否则您会在启动时遇到误按，并且灯会跳到随机亮度。
  • 三个小电容器，可以平滑进入调节器和芯片的功率。
  • 3 针接头，用于离开电路板的仅有的三根电线：电源、接地和连接按钮的电线。

最后你可以看到有很多东西，所以我有了一个绝妙的主意，那就是花费更多的时间和金钱并为其创建 PCB？ 为什么？ 好吧，因为这对于生活中需要类似东西的任何人来说都是有用的，他们只需按一个简单的开关按钮 X 次即可。 我自己需要很多次，例如愚蠢的空调......

另一个原因是因为我从未制作过自己的 PCB，我想学习如何制作以及流程是什么。 第三个原因是因为它真的很酷。 如果你不这么认为，那你就来错地方了。

在 EasyEDA 中进行设计#

正如我所说，我从未使用过这样的东西来制作 PCB，但在学习了一些法学硕士学位后，我决定尝试 EasyEDA。 老实说，这个过程比我想象的要简单得多。 您基本上需要制定一张电路图来解释您需要的所有芯片和东西，然后该工具可以让您显示连接，例如您可以在图像中看到，我将连接标记为“GND”或“3V3”等。每个具有相同名称的连接都将由路由器连接。 整洁的！

然后我基本上必须告诉工具实际的项目是什么。 就像现实生活中的部分一样。 这有助于 PCB 上的定位以及随后的物料清单。

一旦你进行了 PCB 设计，如果你想在上面打印东西，你就可以完全控制事情的走向（我在我的上面打印了一个很酷的开源硬件徽标和我的用户名）。 您还可以控制事物的布线位置、事物的位置、PCB 的形状等等。

您的浏览器不支持视频标签。

我的显然很简单，我只是触及了表面。 它是单层的，我不关心超级复杂的线条，我不必担心线条有多长，或者我是否需要补偿它们的摇摆程度或其他任何东西，但你可以做到这一切，这太酷了！

制作完成#

下一步是去最终为您制造这些 PCB 的公司！ 就我而言，该公司是 JLCPCB。 他们没有赞助这个或任何东西，这只是我最终使用的，说实话，这非常酷，因为你可以在板上选择你想要的现实生活组件，如果你希望他们为你焊接它们，或者如果你乐意自己做。

就我而言，我只需要一块板，而您可以订购的最少数量是 5 个，所以我主要选择自己焊接东西，但对于电容器和电阻器，我选择让他们这样做，因为它们非常小，而且他们这样做的价格可以忽略不计。

然后我下了订单，四天后我手里就拿到了电路板。 老实说，超级简洁，很难用语言来形容，但我想我现在已经上瘾了。 我需要制作更多现实生活中的东西！

对 ATtiny 进行编程#

我立即将其余组件焊接到电线中，并在面包板上的 ATtiny 上测试了我的简单代码，看看它是否有效，结果确实如此。

我实际上使用了 Raspberry Pi 3 来对其进行编程。 空白的 ATtiny 上没有引导加载程序，因此您不能像 Arduino 那样将其插入 USB，它需要一个合适的编程器。 Pi 的 GPIO 引脚可以通过 avrdude 完成这项工作，因此从 Pi 的接头到芯片有 6 根跳线和一个命令。

第一次测试时，我没有将其直接连接到灯上，而是在输出引脚上放置了一个 LED，然后看着它闪烁序列。 眨眼三下，然后就永远没有了（在视频中它实际上眨眼了 4 次，因为我后来才意识到我需要 3 次，哎呀）。

您的浏览器不支持视频标签。

将其焊接到灯上#

然后我把它连接起来，并将其焊接到我的夜灯上。 这很难做到，所有东西都非常小，我的焊接工作也不是我非常自豪的事情，但最终它成功了！

一件奇怪的事情是，板上的大电容器实际上是倒置的，不知道为什么。 幸运的是我用万用表检查了。

有一件事值得在这里大声说出来，因为这盏灯里面没有变压器：一旦我的电路板接线完毕，整个东西就连接到电源了。 这意味着您在插入芯片之前对其进行闪存，并且之后您再也不会将 USB 电缆或 Pi 插入其中。

结果#

在这里您可以看到它所有的荣耀。

您的浏览器不支持视频标签。

“那儿的影子是什么？ 你能看到里面的那些电线吗？ 呃，这个项目很糟糕！”

首先，谁伤害了你？ 其次，我同意，但我不想冒险破坏这些焊点，因为我会哭。 第三，我真的不在乎，我躺在床上，它就亮了。 这些在扩散板后面，它们不会出现在房间的墙上，我是一个快乐的露营者。

现在，当手表告诉我的手机我已经在床上准备睡觉时，手机会告诉家庭助理，它告诉家庭助理打开开关，打开夜灯，然后打开我的混合物，稍微延迟地按下按钮 3 次（以免漏电），它会让我脸上露出灿烂的笑容。

拿走它并制作你自己的#

这一切都在 GitHub 上的 tymscar/button-presser 上，并获得 MIT 许可，所以你可以用它做任何你想做的事。 如果你想要制作这个精确的电路板，那么其中就有 gerbers、材料清单、原理图以及在芯片上运行的几行 C 代码。

自述文件还包含您需要首先执行的两个万用表检查，因为这仅适用于内部具有 4 V 至 12 V 电源轨以及按下时会短路接地的按钮的设备。 这涵盖了很多便宜的小玩意，但不是全部。 如果您的设备像我的设备一样需要电源供电，请在开始之前阅读安全信息。

因此，走出去，为某些东西制作自己的愚蠢的 PCB。 这非常有趣且有益。 下次见！
